articles.title: NFL Power Rankings entering Week 4: The Raiders are 3-0 and there are plenty of signs it might stick
articles.summary: The Raiders have won as many games this season as they did all last season.
articles.body:
NFC East: Cowboys | Giants | Eagles | Commanders NFC North : Bears | Lions | Packers | Vikings NFC South: Falcons | Panthers | Saints | Buccaneers NFC West: Cardinals | Rams | 49ers | Seahawks

AFC East: Bills | Dolphins | Patriots | Jets AFC North: Ravens | Bengals | Browns | Steelers AFC South: Texans | Colts | Jaguars | Titans AFC West: Broncos | Chiefs | Raiders | Chargers

The Las Vegas Raiders had little business hiring one of the hottest head coaching candidates on the market this past offseason. They were an aimless, unserious franchise that hadn't won a division title since 2002.

But Klint Kubiak, coming off helping the Seattle Seahawks to a Super Bowl title as their offensive coordinator, saw the potential when few did.

"There's just a lot to love about this organization," Kubiak said at his introductory media conference in February, via the team's site . "You look around this building and the resources that we have, our meal room, the weight room, the fields outside, the coaches offices, it's as good as it gets in the NFL. Been in a lot of buildings for good reasons and bad reasons, been hired and fired, and the resources are here. We've just got to go put it all together."

In three games, Kubiak has changed the Raiders. Last season was an absolute mess. The team went 3-14 and barely looked like a professional franchise. That wasn't unusual for the Raiders because they had been a mess for years.

Everything looks different this season. Las Vegas made good, smart decisions in free agency. The Maxx Crosby trade famously didn't work out but that is helping the Raiders this season. They had a plan for top draft pick Fernando Mendoza, to sit him and let Kirk Cousins play. The Raiders look like a competent team on both sides of the ball, with a front office making sharp decisions. It has been decades since that was the case.

The Raiders started 2-0 and it was fine to be skeptical, but a 35-27 win at the Saints might be a turning point . The Raiders forced a turnover on all four Saints possessions in the fourth quarter as they came back to win. The 2025 Raiders probably don't win that game. Neither would the 2024 Raiders, 2023 Raiders, 2022 Raiders or most Raiders teams since Bill Callahan's first season (2002), when they won their last playoff game and reached the Super Bowl.

Las Vegas' defense is second in the NFL in EPA allowed per play, a stunning turnaround from last season. The offense is 16th in EPA per play but two of those games came without Brock Bowers , who reminded everyone Sunday, with 116 yards and a touchdown, that he's the NFL's best tight end. Cousins is running a clean operation and the Kubiak influence on the offense is evident.

This weekend might be the biggest game for the Raiders since they moved to Las Vegas, though the team has been there only since 2020. They host the 3-0 Chiefs on Sunday afternoon. The Raiders have won two of their last five games against the Chiefs (one came against Chris Oladokun at QB, not Patrick Mahomes ), but this matchup is different. There's real hope for the Raiders coming into this meeting, not just a fleeting moment that gets washed away with another long losing streak. The Raiders will go into that game feeling confident they can win.

The Raiders are 3-0. And there are no signs yet that it's a mirage.

Here are the NFL power rankings after Week 3 of the NFL season:

The 1976 Buccaneers are the standard for bad teams in NFL history. They went 0-14 with -287 point differential, which is an NFL record. That's -20.5 per game. The 2026 Dolphins are 0-3 with a point differential of -50, which is -16.7 per game. The Dolphins aren't quite on the '76 Bucs' pace, but they're also not an expansion team.

And now Miami will be without running back De'Von Achane , the most talented player on the roster who suffered a season-ending torn ACL in Week 3. And still, Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley is being optimistic. Miami lost by 14 points on Sunday to the Chiefs, but it was a one-score game until the final three minutes.

"That's why this one hurts," Hafley said, via Local10.com. "It's a four-point game in the third quarter. It's a seven-point game with us driving after we got backed up. We got the penalty to get the ball to the 50. I mean, I felt like we were right there."

Cam Ward 's final pass on Sunday was dispiriting. The Giants didn't score a touchdown, so Tennessee's defense did its job. Finally, in the fourth quarter, the Titans' offense woke up and had the ball inside the 10-yard line with a chance to take a lead in the final minute. And on first down, with two timeouts left, Ward had room to run but instead forced a pass that went right to safety Jevon Holland for an interception. Game over.

"He's out in the open, I'd just be smarter with the football," Titans head coach Robert Saleh said . "We've got two timeouts left, it's first-and-goal at the 8, we're going to score, you don't have to force it in that situation. Unfortunately it happened."

Saleh sounded exacerbated. Saleh was asked if Ward would be benched and he said no, but it has to be a consideration if Ward doesn't improve. Ward is 30th among 34 qualified quarterbacks in adjusted EPA ( expected points added ) per play. Last season, he was 52nd of 60. There hasn't been any tangible progress.

The Buccaneers had to know they were taking a risk in going into the season with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels as their backup quarterback . Now Daniels is next in line with Baker Mayfield reportedly out two-to-four weeks with a thumb injury. The Buccaneers have Easton Stick on the practice squad, and at least he has four career starts. The Chargers , however, lost all four of those starts.

The Buccaneers are 2-10 in their last 12 games. They have not covered the point spread in 12 straight games, a record in the Super Bowl era . And now an 0-3 team has to somehow maintain with either an undrafted rookie or a practice squad journeyman at quarterback for maybe a month. Head coach Todd Bowles has to be the favorite to be the first head coach fired .

"Funny thing, we're 0-3 and we're a game out of first place," Bowles told the media after Sunday's game, via Pewter Report . "We have to get our stuff together. We got to reach down and do more. To a coach, to a person, or to a player, we've got to do more."

The Chargers' season has been fascinating. Last week, they matched the 1926 Racine Tornadoes by losing their first two games at home by double digits against teams that had a win percentage of less than .200 the previous season. On Sunday, they forced five turnovers, had a +4 turnover margin and still lost to the Bills. Teams posting those turnover numbers have lost only three times since 2013 and, amazingly, all three times the Chargers have been the losing team, according to Evan Abrams of Action Network.

The Chargers had more than enough breaks to beat the Bills and still somehow trailed 24-13 at the two-minute warning. Even if the Chargers don't feel like the fourth-worst team in the NFL, the results say they are.

At least the Cardinals woke up and realized they should be featuring Jeremiyah Love, the third overall pick of the draft. They gave him 21 of 23 running back carries and he had 90 yards. He added five receptions for 19 yards and a touchdown.

"Left a lot out there, I feel like," Love told ESPN . "I feel like I could help the team a lot more."

The Cardinals didn't play poorly against the 49ers , cutting their deficit to one score three different times in the fourth quarter. With that and a win at the Chargers already, the Cardinals might be a tougher out than expected.

The Jets were practically forced to give rookie first-round tight end Kenyon Sadiq (39% of offensive snaps through two games) a bigger role due to injuries to tight end Mason Taylor and receiver Adonai Mitchell . And Sadiq had a big breakout. He had seven catches for 105 yards and a touchdown. The TD was a fantastic catch in the end zone.

"When you hear the play called in the huddle you know it's got a chance to go to you and then it comes out and you have a man-to-man look," Sadiq said, according to the team's site . "I know Geno [Smith] saw it and I saw it and it's just about going and making a play when your number is called."

The Jets are 1-2 but have been competitive all three weeks. They led in the fourth quarter against the Packers and were tied at Detroit on Sunday, though they lost both games. Developing young players is the main focus of this season. And Sadiq, an athletic freak who was the 16th overall pick, had a very promising showing on Sunday. That's a good sign.

The Panthers have a win over the Falcons when Atlanta was incompetent at quarterback. In their other two games they allowed 59 points to the Bears at home and on Sunday they lost to Deshaun Watson and the Browns .

Bryce Young leads the NFL with 939 passing yards, as he's on pace for more than 5,000. And the win over the Falcons was by 31 points. Maybe that's why the Panthers' start seems better than it actually has been. In reality, Carolina might be 0-3 if they faced a team with a decent quarterback in Week 2. The Panthers could argue that they would be 2-1 if a questionable roughing the passer call on Sunday against linebacker Bobby Okereke didn't wipe out an interception in the last two minutes, but overall the Panthers didn't play well enough to win.

"That's what it comes down to: a couple of red zone and fringe opportunities, came away with field goals and not touchdowns, big difference there," Panthers head coach Dave Canales said, via the team's site . "Missed a few turnover opps early on on the defensive side and gave them an opportunity to continue their drives, some untimely penalties, some things that really hurt us, and we've got to be smarter in some of those areas."

This is as low as the Packers have been ranked in a while. They haven't had a double-digit loss season since 2008. The Packers might not reach 10 losses this season either, but it has been an ugly start.

The defense was OK before it allowed 498 yards on Thursday to the Falcons' Michael Penix Jr., who hadn't played a game in 10 months. Green Bay 's offense is 25th in EPA per play and 30th in success rate, primarily because the offensive line is a mess. Jordan Love has been pressured on 44.4% of his dropbacks, according to PFF , which is a career high. The line isn't doing great blocking for a mediocre group of running backs either. The Packers average a league-worst 3 yards per carry. Head coach Matt LaFleur is on an early hot seat after that awful loss to the Falcons, in part because it's hard to figure out how the Packers turn it around.

"We've got to continue to work with these guys and try to figure out what we do well, because right now I don't know what we're doing well offensively," LaFleur said, via the team's site .

The Texans were 0-3 last season and went 12-5. So Houston can turn this around. But only six teams in NFL history, not counting the 1982 strike season, have made the playoffs after an 0-3 start, according to Josh Dubow of the Associated Press .

"0-3 is where we are right now," Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said, via Texans Wire . "The only way we can do anything about it is to go through it. We're going through it right now, it's adversity, it happens. For me, it starts with me. I have to do a better job of getting our guys ready to roll."

The offense has been a problem. It has failed without Nico Collins , who has missed two games with a hamstring injury. Against a Colts defense that had allowed the most points and yards in the NFL through two weeks, the Texans had 93 yards through three quarters. And 68 of those yards, and seven of their eight first downs, came on one drive. Even with Collins out, it shouldn't have been that hard to sustain drives. QB C.J. Stroud is looking for a contract extension , and the start to this season shouldn't be providing the Texans any optimism that he's worth the massive raise he's seeking.

When the Falcons play with a viable quarterback, they're 1-0 with a dominant road win at Green Bay. Maybe that's how we should judge the Falcons now. The 0-2 start with Cooper Rush mostly doesn't matter because now Atlanta is tied for first place in what again looks to be a putrid NFC South.

Michael Penix Jr. hasn't been a great quarterback yet but he looked phenomenal compared to the Falcons' other QBs. And Penix wouldn't be the first quarterback to break out in his third season. He was 18 of 25 for 256 yards against a Packers defense that had been decent through two weeks, and he provides hope for the offense moving forward.

"He felt comfortable, and that's how he looked," Falcons running back Bijan Robinson said, via the team's site . "He looked comfortable in his game and he was balling."

Drake Maye 's struggles are now alarming . He leads the NFL with six interceptions and has a lost fumble, too. He's 28th in adjusted EPA per play after leading the league in that category last season. There aren't many instances of a quarterback who nearly won MVP in his second season falling this far in his third season, without some major injury involved.

On Monday, head coach Mike Vrabel was asked if he believed Maye was dealing with any lingering effects of a shoulder injury. Vrabel said he wasn't aware of any physical setbacks for his QB. "I think when you go through an NFL game like that, especially as a quarterback, and you get hit, and again, there was not, to my knowledge, anything that would have put him on the injury report or any sort of treatment, " Vrabel said. " … I don't anticipate that being any issue going forward."

The Patriots on the whole look bad. They lost 35-6 to the Jaguars and now just have a narrow home win against the Steelers carrying their résumé.

It's not like the Commanders dominated on Sunday. They were outgained 437-258. They allowed 31 points at home. Marcus Mariota threw for just 183 yards and the Commanders averaged 2.6 yards per rush. That doesn't matter because the Commanders took advantage of all their opportunities to win 33-31, a victory that gives them hope of digging out of an 0-2 hole to start the season.

Also, Jayden Daniels could be close to a return. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn told Albert Breer of The MMQB that Daniels is "more likely than not" to travel to London for the team's Week 4 game against the Colts, which gives him a shot to play two weeks after dislocating his left elbow.

The Browns have two close wins against the Buccaneers and Panthers, who are a combined 1-5 this season with the only win between them coming against a Cooper Rush-led Falcons team. Cleveland was outgained 360-259 by the Panthers at home on Sunday and caught a nice break that Deshaun Watson's late interception was nullified due to a questionable roughing the passer penalty. If you want to buy the Browns' 2-1 start that's fine, but there are not a lot of signs that this is sustainable going forward.

If there is an argument to be made that the Browns can keep this going, it's their defense. After a horrific Week 1 against the Jaguars, the defense has been sixth in the NFL in EPA allowed per play over the last two weeks. Mike Rutenberg took over defensive coordinator job from Jim Schwartz this past offseason and the opening game was concerning, but the group has settled in since then.

The best news for the Colts is that Daniel Jones continues to make progress. A slow start should have been expected as he was returning from a torn Achilles, and he looked rusty at times in the first two games. In Week 3, against a very good Texans defense, Jones completed 24 of 36 passes for 235 yards. He came up with enough plays on the final drive to get Indianapolis in position for a game-winning field goal, after it looked like the Colts might blow a 16-7 lead in the fourth quarter and fall to 0-3. Jones fumbled three times, losing two, but facing defensive end Will Anderson Jr. is tough for any quarterback.

Overall, Jones is progressing. Don't forget how good he was for the first half of last season before the injury.

"Can't turn the ball over like that, costly for the team," Jones said . "Can't put the team in that position and certainly understand how important that is as a quarterback, but the game goes on and you've got to be able to play the next play and execute."

The Saints led the Raiders 27-16 in the second half and it looked like they were on their way to an impressive 2-1 start to the season. But their four fourth-quarter possessions ended with: fumble, interception, fumble, fumble. It's the second time in Saints history they've had four turnovers in a quarter, with the other instance coming in the third quarter of a 1990 game against the Lions, according to Jeff Duncan of the New Orleans Times- Picayune . It was a historic meltdown.

But overall there were some positives. Tyler Shough again looked good with four touchdown passes. Chris Olave had 107 receiving yards. Chase Young had two more sacks. The Saints' 1-2 record belies that they've played good football, and are a failed 2-point conversion at Detroit and a horrible fourth quarter vs. the Raiders from being much higher on this list.

"I think, in many ways, there is a lot of good stuff on this film," Saints head coach Kellen Moore said, according to transcripts . "As painful as this loss is, as frustrating as this loss is, we can't let this thing linger too long. We were in a position to finish that game, and we didn't finish it. We had our opportunities and were not able to get it done. We have to recognize the entire film, not just the ending."

Maybe the Steelers stumbled upon a solution for their offense: Turn Jaylen Warren into a workhorse. Last season, he played 47.4% of the Steelers' snaps, a lower percentage than Kenneth Gainwell . In Week 1, with Rico Dowdle having been added over the offseason, Warren was at 37.3% of snaps. Dowdle was injured in Week 2, and in Week 3 Warren had the backfield to himself. He had 127 rushing yards on 17 carries and 49 receiving yards on three catches. That opened up the Steelers' offense, which hadn't played that well through two weeks. Aaron Rodgers had a strong game with 292 yards and three touchdowns.

Dowdle is considered day to day, but the Steelers have to consider giving Warren a much larger role after what he showed in Week 3.

"Jaylen Warren was dynamic, absolutely dynamic, and guys made some plays down the field," Rodgers said, via the team's site . "Had some explosion in the offense back, especially in the run game."

One image sums up the Cowboys ' loss to the Ravens :

How? The Cowboys completely blew the final 23 seconds. They threw it incomplete on first down, then took a false start before second down. On third down, Dak Prescott, despite plenty of time and no pressure, threw it away instead of waiting for George Pickens, who was wide open. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer confirmed Prescott was throwing it away, for some reason, and took the blame by saying he had been stressing to make sure Dallas didn't blow the field goal opportunity.

"That's on me," Schottenheimer said . "I over-coached him."

After taking the tying field goal, the Cowboys kicked off for a touchback, leaving seven seconds on the clock. That's a bad clock management error because it gave the Ravens enough time to get a completion and a long field goal. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter admitted his team might have decided to go to overtime if there was any less time on the clock.

"Honestly, anything less than seven seconds, it would have been really hard to do the play that we did," Minter said, according to the transcripts. "We may have even just ran the clock out. But [with] seven seconds left, and with the touchback rules, they decided to kick a touchback [and] gave us the ball on the 35. We really only needed 18-plus yards to get to our end-of-game type of range."

The Cowboys might still be good this season, but that loss will linger.

We saw the Giants' limitations on offense Sunday without Jaxson Dart. Against a Tennessee defense that's average at best, New York couldn't score a touchdown. It had 238 yards, with just 118 from Jameis Winston and the passing game. It was a rainy day in New Jersey but it's still unlikely we see much more from the offense going forward.

The Giants made a low-cost trade for J.J. McCarthy on Monday, sending a fifth-round pick to the Vikings for a player who was the 10th pick of the draft just two years ago. It's hard to buy that McCarthy, who has struggled in the NFL, could join the Giants midseason and be the answer. It's more of a developmental trade, and providing depth for later in the season if Winston doesn't turn it around. It's just hard to expect too much, whether it's Winston or McCarthy at quarterback.

The Eagles' 2-0 start was shaky. They barely squeezed out wins over the Commanders and Titans. Philadelphia might have been exposed on Monday night. Its offense was dreadful, barely scoring seven points. Jalen Hurts was poor, and was completely outplayed by Bears 38-year-old third-stringer Case Keenum. Hurts did not look comfortable, and hasn't in the Eagles' new scheme for much of the season. The defense, which had been good but not great during the 2-0 start, was shredded by the aforementioned Keenum, who hadn't taken an NFL regular-season snap since 2023. The Eagles will probably be a good team. They're also pretty close to being 0-3 to start this season. There is a lot that needs to be fixed for the Eagles to get anywhere near an elite level.

The Lions have given up the most points and second-most yards in the NFL this season. They beat the Jets on Sunday but allowed 335 yards and 24 points. Two Jets, Garrett WIlson and Kenyon Sadiq, had 100-yard receiving games. Most Lions games this season will be high scoring. They'll need the defense to make a few plays, like it did in the final minute. The Jets reached the Lions' 28-yard line, but safety Chuck Clark sacked Geno Smith on a blitz, causing a fumble that the Lions recovered.

"And then for our defense to have to, man, they had to make that stop," Lions head coach Campbell said . "That's what it was going to come down to. And it was such a great call by [defensive coordinator] Kelvin Sheppard and those guys executing it."

So much for that notion that the Bengals ' defense is much improved. The Steelers' offense, which ranked 31st in EPA per play through two weeks, had 411 yards and 30 points. The Steelers had only one offensive touchdown through two weeks.

This was a typical Bengals game through the past few years, in which the offense plays well enough to win and the defense isn't good enough. It looked fixed through two weeks, especially in a 20-6 win over Houston. Now all of the old concerns have reemerged. Special teams didn't help either, with a roughing the punter penalty that led to a Steelers touchdown and a muffed punt that gave Pittsburgh three more points.

"Some games you just go get your butt kicked and there's not much to say about it," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said, according to transcripts . "This one, we had our chances. Pittsburgh took advantage of theirs. We didn't take advantage of ours."

Case Keenum will be the feel-good story from the Bears' impressive win over the Eagles on Monday night, and rightfully so. A 38-year-old third-string quarterback played a great game. But the Bears' defense might be much better than expected. In Week 2, they gave up nine points to the Vikings, but that was mostly dismissed because Chicago lost that game. On Monday night the Bears allowed seven points, and had the Eagles' snap on the final play of the first half been a half-second later, it would have been a shutout. If the Bears' defense is even above average, the offense will be very good when Caleb Williams returns, or apparently no matter who is playing quarterback.

Don't forget that the Raiders are winning despite zero snaps from the first overall pick of the NFL Draft, while most other teams are getting immediate contributions from their top-drafted rookie. The plan to have Fernando Mendoza sit and learn hasn't hurt the on-field product yet. The hot start probably means it will be a while before Mendoza plays. It seemed like Mendoza could take over sometime near the midpoint of the season , but it would probably take an immediate losing streak (or an injury to Kirk Cousins, of course) to happen anytime in October.

Mendoza might be sitting for a long time, and the idea that he could sit the whole season is in play. For the 3-0 Raiders, that's for all the right reasons.

The Vikings' offense was bad on Sunday. Starting with the team's second drive of the game, Minnesota had a 10-possession stretch in which it had eight punts, one interception and one touchdown. Kyler Murray was in his first full game in a new system, and he played most of the game without superstar Justin Jefferson after Jefferson left with an ankle injury. Murray had just 168 yards on 29 attempts and had the worst success rate of any quarterback through Sunday's games in Week 3. He was at 21.6%, and the second-worst mark was 28.3%.

It was a poor performance by Murray and the offense but it was also another win.

"It wasn't perfect by any means," Murray said, according to the team's site . "But at the end of the day we're 3-0."

The Broncos got their second straight win against a quality opponent, but there are things to clean up. The Rams had 482 yards to 257 for the Broncos. Denver's offense was awful in the first half, which has been the case in four of the six halves the Broncos have played this season. Offensive coordinator Davis Webb seemed like he might be close to losing play-calling to Sean Payton before the offense started moving in the third quarter. The Broncos made the plays they had to in order to win and deserve credit for that, but a team that has been outgained by 317 yards and outscored by 10 points this season needs to play better, especially in the first half.

"I'm comfortable with the grit of a team that can play well in the fourth quarter," Broncos coach Sean Payton said, according to transcripts. "I'm uncomfortable with how we play at the start of games, if that's a fair answer."

You can't simply dismiss a bad half, because those count too. But if we take out the second half of Jacksonville's Week 2 game against the Broncos — many teams wear down in the second half at Denver's altitude, particularly early in the season — the Jaguars have outscored their three opponents 79-19. Had Jacksonville played a little better against the Broncos in the second half, perhaps their dominant start would be getting more attention. Maybe the Patriots will prove to be a bad team, but they were 14-3 last season and won the AFC, and Jacksonville beat them 35-6 on Sunday. Trevor Lawrence has a 107.8 passer rating this season, and his career high over a full season is 95.2. There are many things to like about the Jaguars' start.

The Jaguars have some tough games coming up (at Bengals, vs. Eagles in London, vs. Texans in London, vs. Colts, at Ravens) but keep your mind open to the Jaguars being one of the NFL's best teams this season.

Dropping the Rams even this far doesn't seem like it will age well. The Rams played on Sunday night at Denver, a team that is 16-4 in its last 20 games, and lost in the final minute after a bad defensive pass interference call . They were without two players who are arguably top 10 non-quarterbacks in the NFL, Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua. It was a reasonable loss. Check the Super Bowl betting odds: The Rams are still favorites at some books, or just behind the Bills. They're 1-2 but don't be fooled into thinking this isn't a very good team. The Rams will be just fine.

Still, 1-2 isn't how the Rams wanted to start . Even if the pass interference call was bad, the Rams were sloppy when it mattered.

The Rams have some things to clean up, and if Nacua and Garrett are out a while it will be a challenge, like it would be for any team losing two players at that level. But listen to the oddsmakers. The Rams will still be a Super Bowl contender.

The Ravens' win over the Cowboys wasn't just dramatic, it was one of a kind. The Ravens' game-winning drive started with seven seconds left, which is the latest a game-winning drive has started after a kickoff since 1978, according to ESPN Insights . It was also the first time in the Super Bowl era that each team made a field goal in the last 10 seconds of regulation, ESPN Insights said.

Lamar Jackson had, not one, but two clutch drives. He took the team 64 yards to score a go-ahead touchdown with 1:30 left and after Baltimore's defense let Dallas tie it, then Jackson hit Zay Flowers on the crucial 27-yard gain that set up the game-winning field goal. He also kept his cool and knew to get a timeout with one second left. The Ravens have blown some games in the fourth quarter the past few years, including one to the Saints in Week 2, but winning like they did Sunday could carry over for a while.

The Chiefs are 3-0 but if there's a concern, it's still the passing offense around Patrick Mahomes. In particular, Xavier Worthy has been surprisingly quiet. In three games, he has 18, 25 and 20 yards. Miami has a poor secondary and Worthy managed only two catches for 20 yards. The hope that the 2024 first-round draft pick could break out in his third season is dwindling.

Other than that, the Chiefs are doing well. The worry is what happens if Kenneth Walker, who is carrying the offense, wears down under the biggest workload of his career or misses time. There's not much else around him for Mahomes to work with.

The Seahawks aren't dropping too far after a loss because it seems unlikely they'll allow 33 points again soon. Seattle allowed only 258 yards, and one of the scores was a pick 6, so the defense will be fine. Sam Darnold should be fine too. He returned from an injury and had four touchdowns, though his two interceptions were a problem.

One troubling aspect is Jadarian Price's start to the season. The rookie first-round draft pick fumbled Sunday and was effectively benched, getting only two more carries after the turnover. He finished with five carries for 15 yards. He has lost a fumble in two straight weeks. The Seahawks can speak positively about the rookie but their actions show they don't fully trust him.

"I think it's as a team, if we turn the ball over, it's not good business," Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said . "I know he didn't come back after the initial fumble; we just decided to calm it down and bring him back after the half. But he's going to be fine. He's going to figure it out; he'll be fine."

The 49ers move up but the injuries are alarming. They lost defensive end Nick Bosa in practice during the week and then receiver Mike Evans and offensive tackle Trent Williams during the game, though it sounds like neither one of those injuries is serious . The 49ers won't get to play the Dolphins and Cardinals every week.

Or maybe everything will be just fine if Brock Purdy avoids the 49ers' weird injury bug. Purdy is playing excellent football, leading the NFL with nine touchdown passes and a sparkling 133.1 passer rating. It's a remarkable run he's on and the main reason the 49ers are 3-0 and second in the power rankings.

The Bills were very sloppy on Sunday. They lost three fumbles and Josh Allen threw two interceptions. Allen, who had been on a phenomenal tear through two games, had a 54 passer rating on Sunday. Not counting Allen's rookie season, he has had a lower passer rating only four times in his career. And despite playing far below average, the Bills were up by 11 points with two minutes left and won by eight.

Allen is unlikely to play that poorly very often this season, and the Bills as a team might not turn it over five times in a game the rest of the season. They didn't turn it over more than three times in game last regular season (they did turn it over five times against the Broncos in a divisional round loss) and hadn't turned it over five times since Week 7 of 2018, when Allen was a rookie. The Bills were at their worst, or very close to it, and still won, which is a good indicator that they're a dominant team.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr.'s Top Potential NFL Landing Spots After Giants Release
articles.summary: Wide receiver-needy teams were given a new option to consider Tuesday in the form of Odell Beckham Jr.
articles.body:
Wide receiver-needy teams were given a new option to consider Tuesday in the form of Odell Beckham Jr.

According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , Beckham and the Giants mutually agreed to part ways Tuesday after OBJ did not record a catch and drew only one target over the season's first three games.

It is unclear how much Beckham has left in the tank, but teams dealing with injuries at wide receiver such as the Los Angeles Rams, Las Vegas Raiders and Carolina Panthers stand out as potential landing spots.

The Rams present perhaps the most natural fit for Beckham since he already has experience with the organization.

L.A. acquired Beckham in a trade with the Cleveland Browns during the 2021 season, and he went on to play a huge role for the team down the stretch and in the playoffs.

Beckham had 27 receptions for 305 yards and five touchdowns in eight regular-season games with the Rams, and 21 grabs for 288 yards and two touchdowns in four postseason contests.

That included two catches for 52 yards and a touchdown in the Super Bowl against the Cincinnati Bengals. Beckham left that game with a torn ACL, but the Rams still went on to win the Super Bowl.

Puka Nacua has missed the Rams past two games with a groin injury, and although head coach Sean McVay told reporters that the Rams are targeting a Week 4 return, nothing is guaranteed.

Without Nacua, quarterback Matthew Stafford has leaned heavily on Davante Adams at wide receiver, and Konata Mumpfield is the only other wideout on the roster to make much of an impact.

The Rams could use some depth at the position, and Beckham's familiarity with McVay and his offensive system could potentially make him an option.

There is no bigger surprise in the NFL this season than the Raiders, who are off to a 3-0 start after picking first overall in the 2026 NFL draft.

Kirk Cousins has been a stabilizing force at quarterback for the Raiders, and he has performed well despite getting little production out of the wide receiver position.

Tight end Brock Bowers did most of the pass-catching work during Vegas' Week 3 win over the New Orleans Saints, and running back Ashton Jeanty has gotten a ton of work as a runner and pass-catcher as well.

As far as wideouts go, Tre Tucker leads the group in receptions (11) and receiving yards (189), while scoring one touchdown.

No other Raiders wide receiver has more than five catches or 52 yards through three games.

On top of that, second-year wideout Jack Bech suffered a broken forearm in the win over New Orleans and will be placed on injured reserve, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

With that, the Raiders' receiving corps is lacking both in terms of depth and talent, so bringing in an experienced wideout like Beckham could go a long way toward at least elevating the floor of the group.

The Panthers won the NFC South last season, and although they are only off to a 1-2 start this season, they are still tied for the lead in their division.

On top of that, quarterback Bryce Young is off to the best start of his young career with an NFL-leading 939 passing yards to go along with seven touchdowns and two interceptions.

Wide receivers Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan have provided Young with some solid production, but Coker left Sunday's road loss to the Cleveland Browns with a quad strain.

According to Rapoport , the strain is considered minor and Coker is questionable to play in Week 4, but this is already the second different injury he has dealt with this season.

The Panthers do not have a wide receiver outside of McMillan and Coker with more than four catches or 83 yards, so depth is a need regardless of Coker's health status.

Beckham could potentially play the role that veterans such as Adam Thielen and Hunter Renfrow did for the Panthers in recent years.

Carolina doesn't have that kind of veteran receiver on the roster this season, so Beckham checks some of the boxes that are currently unaddressed.

articles.title: Giants reportedly releasing WR Odell Beckham Jr. 3 games into his reunion with team
articles.summary: In his regular-season appearances, Beckham was targeted once and didn't record a reception.
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr. 's second go-round with the New York Giants has reportedly come to an end.

The Giants are releasing the 33-year-old Beckham, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo reported Tuesday . Beckham, who became NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year and a three-time Pro Bowler during his first stint in New York, couldn't conjure that form in his late-career homecoming. Although he earned a spot on the 53-man roster this summer and then reclaimed his fabled No. 13 jersey , he didn't make a noticeable on-field impact in his three regular-season games.

In that span, he was targeted once and didn't log a catch. Beckham scattered 20 offensive snaps along the way, with just six of those coming this past Sunday in a 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans , according to Pro Football Focus.

Also on Tuesday, the Giants signed Braxton Berrios to their active roster, per ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Beckham's return to the Giants made for a feel-good story. New York is where he became a star and where he made his iconic ladder-climbing, one-handed grab on "Sunday Night Football" in 2014 .

The former LSU star sat out during the 2025 season, including while he served a six-game suspension from the league for a failed PED test . He also was out of the league in 2022 — after he suffered a torn ACL in his left knee during a Super Bowl LVI victory with the Los Angeles Rams — and resurfaced with the Baltimore Ravens in 2023. That season, he caught 35 balls for 565 yards and a trio of scores.

Then came an unproductive nine-game foray with the Miami Dolphins in 2024. During that stretch, he had nine catches and 55 receiving yards. When a fake social media account reported in August 2025 that OBJ was retiring, he took to X to let everyone know that he was "not done yet."

With the Giants in 2014-18, Beckham accrued 390 receptions, 5,476 receiving yards and 44 receiving touchdowns. Of his five career 1,000-yard receiving seasons, four took place with the organization, which drafted him 12th overall in 2014.

The thought was that Beckham was healthier in 2026 than he has been in years past, plus that his speed work and drop in weight could set him up for renewed success with his old team .

But a promising and nostalgic preseason didn't translate to regular-season numbers. Beckham, who's still the Giants' second all-time leading receiver, was involved sparingly in an offense that's currently reorienting behind backup quarterback Jameis Winston , following the season-ending knee injury Jaxson Dart sustained in Week 2 . The Giants traded for former Minnesota Vikings first-round pick J.J. McCarthy on Monday.

The Cleveland head coach has been in the AFC North for five of the last eight seasons, coaching in some capacity against Watt, either as offensive coordinator for the Ravens or, this season, as the Browns' head coach.

articles.title: Is Brittany Mahomes secretly reading every headline about her? Her Instagram Story sure looks like it

articles.body: Brittany Mahomes has seen the tattoo chatter. And on Tuesday, she answered it. articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers star Cam Heyward may be biased as a defensive linemen, but he's not pleased with some of the defensive penalties that were called during Week 3 of the NFL season.

With penalties called against defenders hitting Patrick Mahomes and Jalen Hurts in particular as the backdrop, Heyward addressed the difficult position defenses are in when facing quarterbacks in the modern game.

"We struggle so much as an NFL when we let quarterbacks play this little game on the sideline instead of either getting the ball out quicker or sliding or just throwing the ball out of bounds," he said during an appearance on The Rich Eisen Show (three-minute mark).

"They have way too many options. But as a defender, he can scurry up the sideline, he can make sure he gets a couple extra yards. I think we've gotta take that out of our game. If they want to get hit, they're going to get hit."

Hurts scurried up the sidelines during a play in Monday's game between his Philadelphia Eagles and the Chicago Bears.

Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson was given an unnecessary roughness penalty for a hard hit he unleashed right as the quarterback was approaching the sideline:

As for Mahomes, a play when the Kansas City Chiefs were deep in their own territory stood out for those upset with some of the calls. Miami Dolphins linebacker Chop Robinson came down on Mahomes with his body weight right after the Chiefs quarterback unleashed a pass from his own end zone and was called for roughing the passer.

"When I saw that clip, I didn't know if it was AI or not because when I saw it, they put a pillow underneath Pat," Heyward joked (1:30 mark).

It may be difficult for defenders, but the NFL is almost always going to lean toward caution when it comes to the quarterbacks. Whether it is landing with body weight during a sack attempt or hitting a running signal-caller near the sidelines, the flags will likely continue to arrive.

articles.title: NFL cuts face-value prices for Commanders-Colts game in London after some fans paid full price
articles.summary: Slow sales reportedly prompted the league to slash price, irking fans who paid full price up front.
articles.body:
Fans who waited to buy Commanders-Colts tickets in London are getting a deal.

Per the Associated Press , the NFL slashed face-value prices of Sunday's game amid slow sales in an effort to fill up the roughly 62,000-seat Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. According to the report, there appeared to be around 2,000 seats still available 10 days before the game when the prices were slashed.

Per the report, the league initially charged up to 245 pounds ($325) for a seat when the tickets initially went on sale. The league recently cut prices on all remaining tickets to 79 pounds ($105), including those in premium seating sections, according to AP. The league is also offering half-price tickets to students, according to the report.

This isn't the first price cut. According to AP, the league previously cut cheaper seats in the upper bowl from 185 pounds ($245) to 115 pounds ($152) prior to the latest price cut to 79 pounds.

Each international game is a showcase for the NFL in its effort to expand its global footprint and fan base. A stadium with noticeably empty seats would be a bad look as the league attempts to sell the appeal of the game to a global audience. Hence the effort to fill seats.

This, of course, has irked fans who paid full price to begin with. London-based NFL fan Andy Burrows railed against the NFL for the move in an interview with AP.

"They don't care about the fans, Burrows told AP, "As long as that place sells out and it looks good on TV, the NFL won't care about us. And I'm not alone. I speak to fans every day."

The NFL did not respond to a request for comment from AP.

Sunday's is the first of three NFL games to be played in London this season. There will also be European games in Madrid, Munich and Paris.

Sunday also marks the 12th NFL game hosted at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. None have previously had an official attendance count below 60,000, according to the report.

Per AP, a Week 5 game between the Philadelphia Eagles and Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium has sold out. A game between the Jaguars and Houston Texans scheduled for Week 6 at Wembley Stadium (NFL capacity 86,000) still has thousands of unsold seats, per the report.

articles.title: Cowboys' Brian Schottenheimer Takes Blame for Mistakes in Ravens Loss After Jerry Jones Remarks
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys' poor clock management near the end of Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens played a major role in their defeat, and head coach Brian Schottenheimer took responsibility for the result Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys' poor clock management near the end of Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Baltimore Ravens played a major role in their defeat, and head coach Brian Schottenheimer took responsibility for the result Tuesday.

"I didn't do very good in the last 28 seconds," he told reporters . "I'll take accountability for it. … I hurt our chances to win that game."

His comments come after Cowboys owner Jerry Jones expressed his frustration with the loss during an appearance on his radio show (h/t Schuyler Dixon of the Associated Press).

Broncos OL Drug Tested After Viral Clip 🎥

"There is no explanation you're satisfied with. None," Jones said. "Let's be sure that we all understand that. They (coaches) don't have one that they're satisfied with. We made mistakes during that time. There's no question about it. So there is no explanation. But there's an evaluation of how not to make the same mistakes again."

Jones also talked to his coach in the aftermath:

It seemed like the Cowboys were going to win when they had 1st-and-goal from the Baltimore 2-yard line with 23 seconds remaining while trailing by three.

However, things turned during a sequence that saw Dak Prescott throw an incompletion, Luke Schoonmaker false start, Schottenheimer call his last timeout after a Prescott scramble and a throw away from the quarterback on the ensuing play.

By the time Brandon Aubrey's field goal tied it, there were just seven seconds remaining.

Yet Aubrey kicked the ball to the end zone on the ensuing kickoff for a touchback that moved the ball to the Baltimore 35-yard line. That gave Lamar Jackson time for one play, and he hit Zay Flowers for 27 yards to set up Tyler Loop's winning 56-yard field goal.

It was a shocking turn of events and one that left the Cowboys with a 1-2 record.

They are tied for last place in the NFC East with the Washington Commanders, although there is still plenty of time to turn things around this season.

"We will be better from this experience that we had with Baltimore and what happened to us at the end of the game," Jones said. "A win would have given you another way of couching it as far as having growth and enthusiasm for having won a game like that because we did come back and we came back in an impressive way. All of that makes us realize we really are just at the beginning of what I hope is an exciting year for us."

Ideally for the Cowboys, the errors near the end of Sunday's loss will be a blip on the radar by the end of a successful season.

Still, it was a difficult defeat to accept in the moment.

articles.title: J.J. McCarthy Unable to Wear No. 9 After Giants Trade, New Jersey Number Revealed

J.J. McCarthy will wear a new number for his new team.

After being traded from the Minnesota Vikings to the New York Giants on Monday, McCarthy appeared on the Giants' roster page as No. 18. He previously wore No. 9 in college and in Minnesota, but that number is occupied by tight end Isaiah Likely.

Of course, the number change means McCarthy will have to find a new alter ego. Last season, McCarthy explained that he channels an alter ego that he called "Nine."

"For me, I call him, 'Nine,' McCarthy said. "Nine comes out, and I got to understand, like, 'OK, he can't be at his peak performance throughout three and a half hours.' So how do I find little ways on the sideline to get back to my breath, get back to my visualization, that can kind of maintain that intense competitive stamina throughout the whole game. But yeah, it's just the pure will and determination to get the job done."

McCarthy had a rough tenure with the Vikings, missing all of his rookie year before throwing for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions last season. The trade gives him a better chance to see the field more and perhaps turn things around following a rocky start to his career.

articles.title: Jalen Hurts Wanted 'Expedited' Concussion Check After Viral Video During Eagles vs. Chiefs
articles.summary: Jalen Hurts explained that he wanted to return to to the field earlier after getting evaluated for a concussion during the Philadelphia Eagles' 27-7 loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday.
articles.body:
Jalen Hurts explained that he wanted to return to to the field earlier after getting evaluated for a concussion during the Philadelphia Eagles' 27-7 loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday.

"I was still waiting," Hurts said after the game, via Michael David Smith of Pro Football Talk. "Just waiting for the thumbs up. I felt fine, we already checked it. I don't know the extent of the process. Obviously wish they could have expedited things. I felt fine."

Hurts exited the contest in the second quarter to be evaluated after getting hit out of bounds while scrambling. He then appeared to be asking to come back in the game.

He eventually returned under center, but it came after backup quarterback Andy Dalton threw an interception that ended Philadelphia's drive.

The Eagles trailed 7-0 and had the ball at Chicago's two-yard line before the turnover occurred.

Hurts returned for Philadelphia's next possession and helped lead a 67-yard touchdown drive to end the first half. The Eagles were ultimately held scoreless throughout the final two quarters of the game, though.

Hurts finished 16-of-25 for 153 yards and one interception. He also rushed for 25 yards and one touchdown.

Under the NFL's concussion and return-to-play protocol , players that are removed from a game to undergo evaluation must complete a concussion assessment before they can return. It includes steps such as a focused neurological exam and a video review.

If any symptoms of a concussion are observed, the player will be escorted to the locker room. Hurts didn't need to enter Philadelphia's locker room on Monday, but still had to wait to clear concussion protocol.

The Eagles fell to 2-1 with the loss as they attempt to advance to the playoffs for the sixth consecutive year.

articles.title: Saints work out 11 free agent offensive linemen, defensive backs
articles.summary: 11 free agents tried out for the New Orleans Saints, almost evenly split between offensive tackles and defensive backs. Here's what you need to know.
articles.body:
Eleven free agents worked out for the New Orleans Saints on Tuesday, according to the daily NFL transactions wire, with a near-even split between offensive linemen and defensive backs. That paints an obvious picture of where the Saints are looking for depth after their first three games. They lost starting left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. to ankle surgery and chose to move on from veteran cornerback Isaac Yiadom , among others, leaving the roster a little thin at two important positions. Rookie safety Lorenzo Styles Jr. is a key special teams player sidelined by injury, and backup corner Martin Emerson Jr. has been unavailable, too.

So let's take a quick look at each free agent who tried out in New Orleans . Two of them were already reported, which we discussed here . These were the four offensive linemen in for a workout on Tuesday:

Cody Ford , Oklahoma. Ford, 29, was a second-round pick by the Buffalo Bills back in 2019 (out of Oklahoma) and has experience at four different offensive line spots. He was most recently a backup right tackle with the Cincinnati Bengals , though he did log 400-plus snaps at left tackle in 2024. He has also started games at both left and right guard. He also served as grand marshal of the Alexandria Mardi Gras parade earlier this year.

Cornelius Lucas , Kansas State. Lucas, 35, spent about a week with the Saints back in 2018 but found his footing as a regular starter with the Washington Commanders from 2020 to 2024. He's a 12-year pro with experience at both tackle spots, though he predominately lines up on the right side (2,878 career snaps) according to Pro Football Focus charting. He played college football at Kansas State and was briefly teammates with Kellen Moore on the Detroit Lions back in the day.

Nicholas Petit-Frere, Ohio State. Petit-Frere, 27, was a third-round pick by the Tennessee Titans back in 2022 and started most of two seasons at right tackle. But he didn't get into a game last season and most recently joined the Washington Commanders for their 2026 training camp. He does have experience at left tackle (starting there in his 2021 senior year at Ohio State) but he's mostly lined up on the right side.

Aamil Wagner, Notre Dame. Wagner, 23 in October, signed with the Titans as a rookie free agent earlier this year and worked at his natural position -- right tackle, where he was a two-year starter for the Fighting Irish. The Saints contacted him a couple of times during the pre-draft process but Tennessee recruited him with $267,500 in contract guarantees (just beneath what the Saints gave Alex Wollschlaegeer and Alan Herron, their highest-paid undrafted free agents).

And here's a look at the six defensive backs:

Tre Hawkins III, Old Dominion. Hawkins, 26, is a tall cornerback at 6-foot-3 and 195 pounds (which helped the New York Giants choose to draft him in 2023's sixth round). He doesn't have much experience covering the slot, and he hasn't seen many snaps on special teams since his rookie year. He spent the final week of the preseason with the Minnesota Vikings .

Jack Henderson, Minnesota . Henderson, 24, played safety and a lot of snaps on special teams since turning pro two years ago (with stops on the Carolina Panthers and Pittsburgh Steelers ). He came up at Southeastern Louisiana before transferring to Minnesota, lining up in the slot on nearly 1,700 snaps in his college career.

Sanoussi Kane , Purdue. Kane, 24, lined up all over the field at Purdue before the Baltimore Ravens picked him in the seventh round of the 2024 NFL Draft. But he mainly played special teams in the NFL before and after the Ravens let him leave their practice squad, at which point he joined the Titans. Tennessee waived him at the start of training camp this summer.

Trevian Thomas, Arkansas State. Thomas earned snaps at Arkansas State (the same alma mater as Demario Davis ) for his work on special teams, and he kept climbing the ladder to win All-Sun Belt recognition in 2024. He has experience covering receivers in the slot and manning the box at the college level, but he hasn't gotten many opportunities in the NFL. He initially signed with the Panthers as a rookie free agent in 2025 before joining the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2026. He may have caught the Saints' eye in a joint practice and preseason game this summer.

Delarrin Turner-Yell, Oklahoma. Turner-Yell, 26, has had some brutal injury luck after the Denver Broncos drafted him with a fifth rounder in 2022. His 2023 season ended with a torn ACL that sidelined him for most of 2025 until he suffered another knee injury in his return to the field. He mostly played free safety in limited action with the Broncos but saw a wider variety of assignments in college.

Marco Wilson , Florida. Wilson, 27, was a three-year starter at Florida before turning pro as a fourth-round pick by the Arizona Cardinals back in 2021. He has spent time with several different teams (most recently the Miami Dolphins during the 2026 preseason), occasionally lining up in the box but primarily covering receivers out on the boundary. He hasn't logged many snaps on special teams.

The Saints have not signed anyone just yet, but stay tuned. They're clearly looking for help at the tackle spots and in the secondary.

articles.title: Bills set to face another banged-up offensive line
articles.summary: Another team with OL injuries before facing the Bills
articles.body:
For the fourth time in as many weeks to begin the 2026 NFL season, the Buffalo Bills defensive line will face an opponent with an injury-plagued offensive line.

The Patriots announced on Tuesday that they've placed veteran right guard Greg Van Roten — who played for the Bills in 2022 — on IR with a thigh injury.

In Week 1 against the Texans, newly signed right tackle Braden Smith wasn't available. In Week 2, the Lions had backup center Juice Scruggs in place of the injured Cade Mays . Left guard Christian Mahogany and rookie first-round right tackle did not play against the Bills.

In Week 3, the Chargers were down to their third-string left guard, rookie center Jake Slaughter was playing his third NFL game as the replacement to Tyler Biadasz , and Cole Strange subbed in for Trey Pipkins at right guard.

Regarding this injury to Van Roten, he was already the replacement for Michael Onwenu . The Patriots starting right guard — who's darn good — fractured his ankle against the Steelers in Week 2 and was subsequently placed on IR.

Ben Brown , a 28-year-old journeyman with 14 career NFL starts and 1,016 snaps since the beginning of 2023, will presumably slide into the right guard spot between second-year pro Jared Wilson at center and grizzled veteran Morgan Moses at right tackle for the club's Week 4 game against the Bills.

Per Fantasy Points Data Suite, Buffalo is sixth in the NFL in defensive pressure rate at 40.3%. Greg Rousseau has played at an All-Pro level through three games. So has Deone Walker .

But we should keep everything in perspective regarding the club's pass rush efforts to date, because the Bills have been afforded the luxury of facing some relatively banged-up offensive lines to begin the 2026 season.

And that theme will continue on Sunday against the Patriots.

articles.title: Colts vs. Commanders bold predictions for NFL London Game in Week 4
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders suddenly have a glimmer of hope for the 2026 season. Meanwhile, the Colts and Sauce Gardner are looking for silver linings. These t...
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders suddenly have a glimmer of hope for the 2026 season. Meanwhile, the Colts and Sauce Gardner are looking for silver linings. These teams will meet in Week 4 of the NFL season, and here are bold predictions for this matchup.

These teams will travel to London to settle the issue. The Commanders will cross the pond with a 1-2 mark after a stunning upset of the Seahawks. As for the Colts , they are 1-2 after their first win. It was a tough 19-17 win over the struggling Texans .

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Commanders QB Marcus Mariota will account for 3 TDs

The Colts have struggled mightily on defense this year. They are the worst in the NFL, allowing 417.3 yards per game. They rank last in pass defense and No. 29 in run defense.

So, part of this prediction is how bad the Colts have been on defense. The other part is that Mariota is more than just a serviceable backup. He's one of the better backup quarterbacks in the NFL.

Against the Seahawks, he went 19 of 31 for 183 yards and three touchdown passes. On the ground, he carried five times for 11 yards. Included in that yardage was a game-clinching run on third down. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said it was special , according to Sports Illustrated.

"I thought there was very little chance Marcus was giving that one off," said Quinn, who gave Mariota a game ball for his performance against the Seahawks. "He has been one of the very best that's ever done it in that space. And so we're all pumped for him. He's a rare teammate, and so that doesn't mean it all goes perfect.

"There was plenty of stuff for us to clean up. We had false starts and procedure issues that we have to get better at. But for him having the ball at the end, that's him and Jay. You're going to put the ball in their hands. As a coach, that's what you think."

Of course, the Commanders will have to get more done on the ground to win consistently. They managed only 82 yards rushing on 32 attempts. That's 2.6 yards per carry, and that won't win a lot of NFL games.

Another thing Mariota did well was spread the ball around. He hit nine different receivers, including Terry McLaurin , Treylon Burks , and Rachaad White for scores.

Look for Mariota to get a couple of passing scores against the Colts while also finding a seam for a rushing score.

Commanders WR Treylon Burks will find the end zone again

This is the epitome of a bold prediction. Burks has just two catches on three targets for the season. He has a total of 13 receiving yards. But if Jayden Daniels hadn't overthrown him against the Cowboys, he would already have two touchdowns.

Burks has a big body and good speed. When he's healthy, he can get open. The Commanders aren't going to pepper him with targets, but that's why he has a chance to score. The defense won't be concerned about him. And he's big enough and strong enough to score.

Burks worked hard this offseason, and his health stayed with him, according to TheBanner.com.

"Honestly, I feel like this was the first offseason where I haven't had to battle back from an injury," Burks said. "I've never lost confidence in myself. I just want to keep getting better.

"Last year brought the fun back of playing football, for me. (General manager) Adam (Peters) and Dan Quinn made it feel like home."

Peters said earlier this year that Burks still has untapped potential.

"I think he has another level to go to," Peters said. "He showed us a lot in practice and in the games when he was able to make some plays there."

Colts RB Jonathan Taylor will have 100 total yards, 2 TDs

It's going to be a tough task for the Commanders to contain Taylor. He hasn't topped the 100-yard mark rushing this year, but had 98 and 92. However, he had 132 and 121 total yards in the first two games before the Texans' tough defense held him to 72.

The Commanders have been excellent against the run. They've allowed only 82 yards per game to rank No. 3 in the NFL. However, this is a different animal against Taylor. And the Colts won't be afraid to employ Taylor in the passing game against the Commanders, who rank No. 31 in the NFL by allowing 280.3 yards per game through the air.

The Colts know they go as Taylor goes. They will feed him the ball, one way or the other. And look for them to have more running success than they did against the Texans. The Commanders are good versus the run, but they aren't the Texans.

Colts head coach Shane Steichen won't get away from Taylor because he knows too much about what he brings , according to a post on X by Jake Arthur via aol.com.

"When you're in the moment of the game, you're just playing the game, coaching the game," Steichen said. "But after you look back and watch the tape and the stuff that he puts out, the numbers he's put up throughout his whole career have been awesome. And obviously, we want to continue that trend this year with him."

articles.title: Cowboys coach on brutal ending against Ravens: ‘I didn’t do very good’
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys faced the Baltimore Ravens in Rio as part of the NFL’s international series, and the game delivered one of the most exciting endings of th...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys faced the Baltimore Ravens in Rio as part of the NFL's international series, and the game delivered one of the most exciting endings of the young NFL season. Trailing by three late in the game, the Cowboys drove the length of the field but were stuffed at the goal line, forcing Dallas to settle for a game-tying field goal with seven seconds left on the clock.

A touchback on the ensuing kickoff put the ball at the Baltimore 35-yard line. However, rather than settling for overtime, the Ravens offense found a way to win in regulation. Two-time NFL MVP Lamar Jackson hit Zay Flowers over the middle against a soft Cowboys defense to get the ball to the Dallas 38-yard line. As Flowers went to the ground, Jackson was calling for the timeout, and after a brief huddle, the refs determined that there was still a second left on the clock.

On Tuesday, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer took ownership of the brutal finish.

"I didn't do very good in the final 20 seconds (of Sunday's game in Rio)," he said via The Athletic's Jon Machota. "I hurt our chances to win that game. I'm better than that. … Those things won't happen again."

After the loss, Pardon Interruption's Michael Wilbon made it clear he felt that the embarrassing end to Friday's game was right on par for the Cowboys' franchise.

"Dallas is dumb every year," Wilbon said . "It doesn't matter what they do to their offense and defense… they just seem intellectually challenged, no matter who's running that outfit." Just three weeks into the season, the Cowboys are already behind the 8-Ball."

For his part, outspoken Cowboys owner Jerry Jones made it clear he didn't have a fitting explanation for how things played out in Brazil.

"There's no explanation that you're satisfied with," Jones said. "None. Let's be sure that we all understand that. They don't have one that they're satisfied with. We made mistakes during that time, there's no question about it. There's no explanation. There's an evaluation of how to not make the same mistakes again, which is what you should be doing. We can't get that back. No way to get it back. What you can do is use it — if there's any aspect of it that you want to just not even think happened. Any aspect of it, use it to get better."

The Cowboys will get a chance to put the loss behind them in Week 4 against the Houston Texans .
